newsitem.title: GERMANY: Airlines formalize alliance, seek partners.
newsitem.headline: Airlines formalize alliance, seek partners.

text.p: A group of major airlines, including Germany's Deutsche Lufthansa AG and United Airlines, said Wednesday their partnership would be known as "Star Alliance," but said no mergers would take place.
The alliance, in addition to Lufthansa and United, includes Air Canada, Scandinavian Airlines Systems and Thai Airways International Ltd.

The branding deal, a bid to cut costs and offer integrated travel for passengers and cargo, creates one of the largest industry alliances and rivals that announced last year by British Airways and American Airlines.
Other airlines are expected to join the expanding group, among them Brazil's Varig Airlines, which said Wednesday it will join in October.
The partners said other potential partners include South African Airways and regional European carrier British Midland, which both now cooperate with Lufthansa.
Talks also were being held with unidentified Asian airlines to strengthen the alliance's presence in the expanding region, but alliance airline executives declined to comment.
The airlines, which have been working closely for a few years, said they would not take equity stakes in one another and each airline would retain its individual identity.
The five airlines have a combined staff of more than 210,000 employees and flights to 578 cities in 106 countries.
The partners projected annual global passenger growth of 5 percent to 6 percent in the coming years and Lufthansa said cargo shipment growth would average 6 percent to 7 percent.

The partnership calls for common branding in marketing and advertising, coordination of routes, offering of code-share flights and further integration of some airport operations, purchasing and ticketing operations.
Passengers also will be able to accumulate and redeem mileage points on any of the partner airlines.

The airlines said they did not expect the partnership to violate regulatory anti-competition laws. They noted that anti-trust immunity already exists for the relationship between United, Lufthansa and SAS in the United States and immunity for United's alliance with Air Canada is pending among regulatory authorities.
The European Union is still investigating the alliance, but the carriers said in the statement that they did not expect any problems from the review by Brussels.
